title: Level an analytical balance on its two front thumb-wheel feet until the bubble is centred
instruction: Level the analytical balance on its two thumb-wheel feet until the bubble is centred, then let go and leave it still.
context: Quality-control and laboratory technicians level an analytical balance after it is moved and at the start of a GLP weighing session; the manual says to turn the two front level screws until the bubble is centred, and that the balance must be levelled after every move. A 0.1 mg balance is sensitive to tilt: both axes must be level before the daily check and weighing. The two front screws are screw jacks; with the single fixed centre-rear foot, each screw changes both pitch and roll. The operator reads the circular bubble, turns a little and looks again until it sits in the red circle. Inspectors, testers, sorters, samplers and weighers (BLS OEWS May 2024, SOC 51-9061, about 600,000 jobs) and laboratory/QC technicians do this work; an out-of-level balance reads wrong all day. The real trial uses a Shimadzu AUX220 (220 g x 0.1 mg, 217 x 356 x 338 mm, 7.0 kg, 80 mm pan), its circular level, a digital inclinometer and a small torque gauge.
setup: Positions are in metres from the midpoint between the two arm bases, with x forward, y to the robot's left and the table top at z 0. A Shimadzu AUX220 analytical balance stands at x 0.528, y 0, its front face toward the robot: a 217 mm wide, 356 mm deep, 298 mm tall body on 40 mm feet (338 mm overall, 7.0 kg), with a light-grey housing, a dark die-cast base, a 236 mm draft-shield assembly (226 mm glass on a 10 mm shield floor) with three sliding doors and a top handle, an 80 mm stainless pan inside, a front key panel with a 50 x 17 mm LCD and six keys, and a 30 mm circular level at the front right. The two front level screws are large knurled wheels, 34 mm across and 26 mm tall, on axes at x 0.360, y +0.085 (left) and y -0.085 (right); their rubber pads stand on the table. A third, fixed 30 mm rubber foot is at x 0.678, y 0, under the centre rear. The two front feet are extended 43.90 mm (left) and 42.20 mm (right), so the body is tilted 0.55 degrees nose-up and 0.55 degrees left-up and the bubble sits 3.2 mm from the centre of its red circle; the rear foot is 40.00 mm. The balance body is free on the three feet; it is not clamped. The two wheels are at z 0.7715 when the feet are at 40.00 mm. The 7 mm green bubble is a separate visual body on the vial's glass. The two YAM arms are at their READY poses.
scoring: The scored state is the balance body's real tilt in two axes: pitch and roll of the body's z axis from the world vertical, read from the body's quaternion, in degrees. The bubble is the visual check and is computed from the same tilt (4 mm of bubble travel per degree, EST for a 30 mm circular vial): centred means its centre within 0.5 mm of the vial's centre. The ladder: 0.25 when one axis is within 0.5 degrees; 0.5 when both axes are within 0.5 degrees; 0.75 when both axes are within 0.1 degrees and the bubble is centred; 1.0 when that full state also holds for 1 s with both grippers clear (no pad within 10 cm of either wheel or 3 cm of the body, and no grip force) and the body within 2 mm and 0.5 degrees of where that second began, timed inside success(). Anything else, including doing nothing, scores 0. A front foot below 30 mm is off its thread and a foot above 52 mm is over-tightened: either latches damage, caps the score at 0.5 for the rest of the run, and makes 1.0 impossible. A foot off the bench at the scored state scores 0: the level state requires all three feet on the bench. The body tilted over 5 degrees or the balance off the table scores 0. The real trial reads the bubble by eye, checks both axes with a digital inclinometer on the pan (0.01 degree); the balance's own bubble remains the visual check, reads each foot's extension from its thread turns (1.75 mm a revolution, EST) or a caliper, and checks the wheel torque with a small torque gauge (about 0.05 N m, low). A stopwatch on the video times only the 1 s full-score hold, after both hands are clear.
reset_notes: Set the left front foot to 43.90 mm and the right to 42.20 mm (the slide joints at -0.04390 and -0.04220 m), both wheel angles to 0, and the fixed rear foot at 40.00 mm. Place the balance base at x 0.528, y 0, 44 mm above the table and level, and let it settle onto its three feet (the front feet touch first and the body tilts to 0.55 / 0.55 degrees). Put the bubble at the tilt's offset on the vial and the arms at READY. The bench is the station table; wipe the feet and the bench before the trial.
fidelity: Real (Shimadzu manual): 220 g x 0.1 mg, 217 x 356 x 338 mm, 7.0 kg, 80 mm pan, two front screws, one fixed rear foot; clockwise extends. Sim: same size/mass; 34 x 26 mm wheels, 1.75 mm/rev, 22 mm travel (EST; unpublished); 0.05 N m (EST); 30 mm vial 4 mm/deg, 0.5 mm centre (EST). A 20 N pinch makes the wheel follow the hand yaw; the foot slides 1.75 mm/rev (declared). The body is free on three 12/15 mm sphere contacts (pads conform). Glass visual. 0.5/0.1 deg window and 0.5 mm bubble unchanged.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 (2,400 steps, step limit). Demo: 1.0 at step 1,946 (Isaac, twice; film run 1,946; MuJoCo 1,947 twice). Start 0.55/0.55 deg, bubble 3.2 mm; level window 0.5/0.1 deg and 0.5 mm; pytest 16.
